subject: Chemistry
title: Why Candles Flicker
description: A quick, practical guide to Why Candles Flicker.

hook.text: A candle flame is a tiny chemical factory performing thousands of reactions every second.

buildup.text: The wick draws liquid wax upward by capillary action. Heat vaporizes the wax into a gas.

discovery.text: Wax vapor mixes with oxygen and combusts. The yellow glow comes from tiny soot particles heated white-hot.

twist.text: The blue base of the flame is the hottest part—up to 1,400°C. The yellow tip is cooler.

climax.text: Michael Faraday gave six lectures about candle chemistry in 1848. He called it 'the best science lesson.'

punchline.text: A candle: liquid to gas to light. Combustion you can hold.

quiz.question: What makes a candle flame glow yellow?
options: Tiny soot particles heated to white-hot temperatures
The chemical color of burning wax
Reflected light from the melted wax pool

details.summary: A candle flame flickers because convection currents caused by the flame's own heat create turbulent airflow patterns. The combustion of vaporized paraffin wax produces a complex reaction zone where solid carbon particles incandesce, creating the visible yellow glow.
details.whyItMatters: Candle chemistry involves vaporization, combustion, and radiation in a self-sustaining system. Studying it has advanced understanding of diffusion flames used in industrial burner design.
takeaways: The wick draws liquid wax upward through capillary action
Yellow flame color comes from incandescent carbon soot particles
Flickering results from turbulent convection around the flame

faq.question: Why is the base of a candle flame blue while the top is yellow?
faq.answer: The blue zone at the base has abundant oxygen, producing complete combustion. Higher up, oxygen is limited, causing incomplete combustion that creates tiny carbon soot particles. These particles glow yellow-white when heated, producing the characteristic warm color.

faq.question: Why do candles in zero gravity burn differently than on Earth?
faq.answer: Without gravity, there is no convection to draw fresh air to the flame or carry away combustion products. Space candle flames form spherical blue shapes and burn more slowly because oxygen can only reach the flame through diffusion.
